profile.reading: This Csquare facility is in the Santa Clara/Sunnyvale, California area, part of the Silicon Valley market. Csquare, the same operator recorded elsewhere in this registry under the name Centersquare (centersquaredc.com redirects to csquare.com), states on its own site that it runs 80 colocation data centers across 30 markets, totaling 3.5 million square feet of space and more than 500 megawatts of power capacity, serving over 2,000 customers, and describes having operated for over 20 years. The company is headquartered at 3100 Olympus Boulevard, Suite 510, Coppell, Texas. No detailed founding history, prior company names, ownership structure, or building specific address and MW figures for this particular row were confirmed in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO1 publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara. The published figure is utility power, not IT load, and the operator does not publish a separate IT load or power usage effectiveness value, so translating directly to rack count requires an assumption: at 10 kW per rack, a conservative colocation density, 129.4 MW of utility power might support on the order of 10,000 to 13,000 racks after typical losses, while at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that same utility figure might yield roughly 2,500 to 3,200 racks depending on overhead. Neither number is the operator's claim. The 273,000 square feet of technical space is large enough that high-density AI deployments would use a fraction of the floor while consuming most of the power budget.

The six certifications define the compliance envelope the campus can serve. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for financial and operational controls audits. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data workloads. ISO 27001 establishes a certified information security management framework. NIST 800-53 aligns the facility with federal security controls, which is relevant to government or regulated-sector tenants. LEED indicates a recognized sustainability standard for the building. No tenant information is published.

In California context, this site is one of 103 facilities mapped in the state, and only 7 of those publish a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. The 7 facilities with published figures sum to 185 MW in this site's data. At 129.4 MW, SFO1 ranks eighth by published capacity among California facilities in this dataset, which means it accounts for the majority of the 185 MW total on its own and exceeds the combined remainder. That concentration reflects how few California operators publish capacity figures, not necessarily the true distribution of power across the state.
